title: Constellations
standard_text: Stars form patterns called constellations, which appear to move across the sky because of the Earth's rotation and change with the seasons because of the Earth's revolution. Filipino farmers and sailors used stars to mark planting time and find directions. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 6, Quarter 4: Earth and Space)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Earth and Space): constellations, why stars seem to move, stars and their colors, galaxies and the night sky. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A constellation is a pattern of stars.
key_sub: Stars seem to move because the Earth rotates.
body_html:
How to think about it

A constellation is a group of stars that forms a pattern, such as Orion, the Southern Cross (Crux) and Scorpius. Stars seem to rise in the east and set in the west because the Earth rotates; we see different constellations in different months because the Earth revolves around the Sun.

Stars are huge balls of hot gas; their colors show their temperature. Our Sun is one star among billions in the Milky Way galaxy. Long ago, Filipinos watched certain stars, such as the Pleiades, to know when to plant rice.

Example

Which constellation has three stars in a row as a belt?

A hunter

Answer: Orion

Example

Why do stars seem to move at night?

The Earth spins.

Answer: the Earth rotates

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the stars in a constellation are close together in space.
  • Thinking stars only come out at night (they are there in the day too).
  • Thinking all stars are the same color.

faq.q: Why can we see more stars in the province than in the city?

faq.a: They used the positions of stars to find directions at night.

items.q: Light from the sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. Light from Arcturus takes 37 years. Why does the sun look so much brighter?
c: The sun is the only star that gives off light.
The sun is much, much closer to Earth.
Arcturus is a planet, not a star.
The sun is the biggest star in the universe.
items.e: The sun is about 8 light-minutes away; Arcturus is 37 light-years away. Distance makes the difference.

items.q: What is a constellation?
c: a pattern of stars in the night sky
items.e: The Big Dipper is part of Ursa Major.

items.q: Which constellation, the Southern Cross, can be seen low in the southern sky from the Philippines?
items.e: It is small and shaped like a cross.

items.q: Why do the stars seem to move across the night sky?
c: the Earth rotates on its axis
items.e: Stars rise in the east and set in the west, like the Sun.

items.q: Which constellation looks like a scorpion with a curved tail?
items.e: It is seen in the evening from about May to August.

items.e: The rising of certain stars marked the planting season.
